modules.name: architecture
modules.offer: The project has (or will have) a codebase — stack, layout, commands, external services.

modules.name: environments
modules.offer: Something runs or deploys somewhere — environments, access, deploy procedure.

modules.name: client
modules.offer: Work is delivered to a client or external stakeholder — contacts, commercial state, expectations.

modules.name: automations
modules.offer: The project owns automations, routines, or integration glue — inventory of what runs where.

modules.name: working-docs
modules.offer: The project produces long-form working material — investigation write-ups, playbooks, plans, specs — that needs a durable home.

strategies.merge-blocks: If dest exists: keep ALL existing content, append the proto-marked blocks (and only them) below it; never duplicate a block that already exists (match by marker name). If dest absent: copy whole file.
strategies.copy-if-absent: Copy only if dest does not exist. On collision: skip and report — never overwrite.

module_selection: Modules are independent and à la carte — no bundles. proto-init proposes each module whose `offer` line matches what it learned about the project (type, codebase scan, interview answers); the user confirms the final set. Zero modules is valid.

removed_blocks.name: external-conventions
removed_blocks.disposition: delete — its principle line lives in the 'Convention pointers' section
